title: Elazar ben Pe’irah
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman says that his name remained an everlasting disgrace and reproach: through him Yochanan the High Priest became a Sadducee and killed the sages of Israel. He cites Kiddushin 66a: in the days of King Yannai (whom Hyman identifies here as Yochanan), the king had a friend, a scoffer, evil-hearted and worthless, named Elazar ben Pe’irah. Hyman identifies him with the Elazar ben Patora named in Jerusalem Talmud Sotah 9:11, where Yehudah ben Pakhora is also named, “priests of…” [The supplied notice ends here.]

notes.text: The supplied text ends with the incomplete כהני (“priests of…”). Its לא אוהב is also irregular; the translation reads the intended friend relationship without silently correcting the Hebrew. Hyman’s identification of Yannai with Yohanan is retained as his.

No new primary scalar was returned. The disgrace, Sadducee conversion, killing and identification of Yannai with Yochanan are attributed to Hyman rather than newly established history. The supplied לא אוהב is contextually read as a friend, corresponding to לו אוהב, but the literal letters are retained here as an unresolved source question, not a proven print repair. Pe’irah, Patora and Pakhora remain distinct forms. The final כהני is an incomplete construct, priests OF; no community or continuation is invented.

Hyman’s print (vol. I, pp. 199–200) reads היה לו אוהב, “he had a friend,” where the supplied Hebrew has לא אוהב. The printed notice continues after the supplied cutoff with בעלי אגרופין, referring to men who used force. Hyman then disputes another account of their role and states his identification with the Kiddushin figure as beyond doubt. The consulted Jerusalem Talmud passage names Elazar ben Paḥora and Yehudah ben Pakhora and describes their taking portions by force. The identification with the court figure in Kiddushin remains Hyman’s.
